key_insight: MLP-mixer neural wave functions offer lightweight information mixing, while a hierarchical mixer–transformer architecture outperforms compared models on large quantum systems.
engineering_relevance: These architectures could improve the accuracy–cost trade-off in classical simulations of quantum many-body ground states.
method: Use an MLP mixer as a neural wave-function ansatz to mix information globally and locally.
Combine the mixer with a transformer in a hierarchical architecture.
Compare against RNNs and transformers using single-site and patched inputs.
evidence_signal: Ground-state benchmarks on two-dimensional quantum many-body systems across phases and sizes evaluate representational accuracy and computational efficiency, reporting competitive mixer performance and stronger large-system results for the hierarchical model.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical accuracy gains, runtime measurements, or resource requirements, so practical scalability needs verification.
paper_title: Scalable Neural Wave Functions via Information Mixing and Hierarchical Network Architectures
